claims.text: The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and the selected equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets have single-phase FCC microstructures after identical thermomechanical processing.
Local lattice distortion and microstrain vary among the quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys.
Atomic-size mismatch and solute arrangement generate local lattice distortions and associated microstrain fields.
Local lattice distortion and microstrain vary nonlinearly with constituent count.
Changes in local lattice distortion alter local stress fields.
Altered local stress fields modify dislocation nucleation.
Altered local stress fields modify dislocation mobility and interactions.
Differences in dislocation nucleation, mobility, and interactions produce variations in yield strength, work hardening, and failure response.
Constituent count alone cannot explain the alloys' differing deformation and failure behavior.
The quaternary and ternary alloys will show XRD peak-broadening and microstrain signatures distinct from those of the quinary baseline.
Differences in diffraction and microstrain signatures will correlate with differences in dislocation behavior and mechanical properties.
The quinary alloy has a characteristic level of local lattice distortion associated with its work-hardening and failure behavior.
High-resolution XRD, synchrotron diffraction, and HRTEM can be used together to quantify or assess lattice distortion and microstrain.
The comparison will use matched room-temperature loading conditions, strain rates, grain size, and thermal history.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to room-temperature deformation at controlled strain rates in identically processed, single-phase FCC specimens.
Diffraction methods alone may not resolve subtle microstrain differences because of detection limits.

Statistically equivalent lattice-distortion and microstrain measurements across compositions, together with significantly different mechanical responses, would falsify the proposed mediation mechanism.
